claim: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are attractive candidates to combat antibiotic resistance for their capability to target biomembranes and restrict a wide range of pathogens.
source: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are attractive candidates to combat antibiotic resistance for their capability to target biomembranes and restrict a wide range of pathogens.
evidence: This is a general statement about AMPs supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: The study established a de novo AMP design framework by bridging a deep generative module and a graph-encoding activity regressor.
source: Here, we establish a de novo AMP design framework by bridging a deep generative module and a graph-encoding activity regressor.
evidence: This describes the methodology developed in the study.

claim: The study discovered 16 bifunctional AMPs that were experimentally validated for their abilities to inhibit a spectrum of pathogens in vitro and in animal models.
source: We discovered 16 bifunctional AMPs and experimentally validated their abilities to inhibit a spectrum of pathogens in vitro and in animal models.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: P076 is a highly potent bactericide with the minimal inhibitory concentration of 0.21 μM against multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
source: Notably, P076 is a highly potent bactericide with the minimal inhibitory concentration of 0.21 μM against multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii
evidence: This is a specific experimental result from the study.

claim: P002 broadly inhibits five enveloped viruses.
source: while P002 broadly inhibits five enveloped viruses.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: The World Health Organization (WHO) has projected a looming health threat of 10 million casualties per year by 2050 due to antimicrobial resistance.
source: Due to increasing cases of untreatable bacterial infections, the World Health Organization (WHO) has projected a looming health threat of 10 million casualties per year by 2050 (Murray et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Murray et al., 2022.

claim: The WHO has identified six antimicrobial-resistant pathogens (Enterococcus faecium, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterobacter species) as ESKAPE.
source: Specifically, the WHO has identified six antimicrobial-resistant pathogens (Enterococcus faecium, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterobacter species) as ESKAPE.
evidence: This is established knowledge about WHO classification of pathogens.

claim: The ESKAPE pathogens have severely limited the treatment options for serious infections and impaired the conditions of immunodeficient patients.
source: The ESKAPE pathogens have severely limited the treatment options for serious infections and impaired the conditions of immunodeficient patients (De Oliveira et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to De Oliveira et al., 2020.

claim: The majority of clinically available antibiotics were developed more than 30 years ago.
source: In sharp contrast, the majority of clinically available antibiotics were developed more than 30 years ago (Hutchings et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hutchings et al., 2019.

claim: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are cationic macromolecules usually 10–60 amino acids in length.
source: As a naturally evolved defense line of innate immune system, antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are cationic macromolecules (usually 10–60 amino acids) widely present in all living organisms (Huan et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge about AMPs supported by citation.

claim: AMPs are widely present in all living organisms.
source: As a naturally evolved defense line of innate immune system, antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are cationic macromolecules (usually 10–60 amino acids) widely present in all living organisms (Huan et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge about AMPs supported by citation.

claim: AMPs effectively inhibit a wide range of pathogens, such as Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, fungi, and viruses.
source: AMPs are attractive alternatives to conventional antibiotic treatment because they effectively inhibit a wide range of pathogens, such as the Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, fungi, and viruses (Huan et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge about AMPs supported by citation.

claim: The majority of AMPs feature amphiphilic patterns of amino acid sequences and enriched positive charges.
source: The majority of AMPs featured amphiphilic patterns of amino acid sequences and enriched positive charges (e.g., lysine and arginine residues), which allowed AMPs to disrupt the membrane components and exert antimicrobial effects (Mahlapuu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about AMP structure supported by citation.

claim: AMPs disrupt membrane components and exert antimicrobial effects.
source: The majority of AMPs featured amphiphilic patterns of amino acid sequences and enriched positive charges (e.g., lysine and arginine residues), which allowed AMPs to disrupt the membrane components and exert antimicrobial effects (Mahlapuu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about AMP mechanism supported by citation.

claim: Development of resistance to AMPs was a rare event even after 100 passages of lab evolutions.
source: Due to the relative constant compositions of biological membranes as the essential AMP targets, development of resistance to AMPs was a rare event even after 100 passages of lab evolutions (Spohn et al., 2019; Huang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Spohn et al., 2019 and Huang et al., 2023.

claim: Naturally evolved and rationally designed AMP sequences (~20,000) are housed in several databases paired with experimentally validated activities.
source: Notably, the naturally evolved and rationally designed AMP sequences (~20,000) are housed in several databases (APD [Wang et al., 2016], DBAASP [Pirtskhalava et al., 2021], DRAMP [Shi et al., 2022], etc.) and paired with experimentally validated activities (minimal inhibitory concentration [MIC]), thus facilitating data mining endeavors for more diverse sequences and more effective peptides (Xu et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to database papers.

claim: Deep learning models have led to the discovery of highly efficient AMPs with MIC of 2 μM against Escherichia coli.
source: Indeed, deep learning models have led to the discovery of highly efficient AMPs (e.g., MIC of 2 μM against Escherichia coli).
evidence: This is a general statement about the field supported by established knowledge.

claim: Deep-AMPEP30 utilized deep convolutional networks to learn and recognize latent representations of meaningful peptides.
source: Specifically, predictive models like Deep-AMPEP30 (Yan et al., 2020), AMPlify (Li et al., 2022), TransImbAMP (Pang et al., 2022), and sAMPpred-GAT (Yan et al., 2023) utilized deep convolutional, recurrent, attention-based, and graph neural networks to learn and recognize latent representations of meaningful peptides.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yan et al., 2020.

claim: AMPlify utilized recurrent networks to learn and recognize latent representations of meaningful peptides.
source: Specifically, predictive models like Deep-AMPEP30 (Yan et al., 2020), AMPlify (Li et al., 2022), TransImbAMP (Pang et al., 2022), and sAMPpred-GAT (Yan et al., 2023) utilized deep convolutional, recurrent, attention-based, and graph neural networks to learn and recognize latent representations of meaningful peptides.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Li et al., 2022.

claim: TransImbAMP utilized attention-based networks to learn and recognize latent representations of meaningful peptides.
source: Specifically, predictive models like Deep-AMPEP30 (Yan et al., 2020), AMPlify (Li et al., 2022), TransImbAMP (Pang et al., 2022), and sAMPpred-GAT (Yan et al., 2023) utilized deep convolutional, recurrent, attention-based, and graph neural networks to learn and recognize latent representations of meaningful peptides.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Pang et al., 2022.

claim: sAMPpred-GAT utilized graph neural networks to learn and recognize latent representations of meaningful peptides.
source: Specifically, predictive models like Deep-AMPEP30 (Yan et al., 2020), AMPlify (Li et al., 2022), TransImbAMP (Pang et al., 2022), and sAMPpred-GAT (Yan et al., 2023) utilized deep convolutional, recurrent, attention-based, and graph neural networks to learn and recognize latent representations of meaningful peptides.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yan et al., 2023.

claim: Deep learning models enabled comprehensive mining of the human gut microbiome for AMPs.
source: These models recently enabled comprehensive mining of the human gut microbiome (Ma et al., 2022), modern and ancient human proteomes (Maasch et al., 2023; Torres et al., 2022), or even the entire sequence space of hexapeptides (Huang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ma et al., 2022.

claim: Deep learning models enabled comprehensive mining of modern and ancient human proteomes for AMPs.
source: These models recently enabled comprehensive mining of the human gut microbiome (Ma et al., 2022), modern and ancient human proteomes (Maasch et al., 2023; Torres et al., 2022), or even the entire sequence space of hexapeptides (Huang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Maasch et al., 2023 and Torres et al., 2022.

claim: Deep learning models enabled comprehensive mining of the entire sequence space of hexapeptides for AMPs.
source: These models recently enabled comprehensive mining of the human gut microbiome (Ma et al., 2022), modern and ancient human proteomes (Maasch et al., 2023; Torres et al., 2022), or even the entire sequence space of hexapeptides (Huang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Huang et al., 2023.

claim: PepVAE reconstructed sequences from latent space according to the encoder-decoder architecture of variational autoencoders.
source: Generative models like PepVAE (Dean et al., 2021), CLaSS (Das et al., 2021), and HydrAMP (Szymczak et al., 2023) reconstructed the sequences from latent space according to the encoder-decoder architecture of variational autoencoders (VAEs)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dean et al., 2021.

claim: CLaSS reconstructed sequences from latent space according to the encoder-decoder architecture of variational autoencoders.
source: Generative models like PepVAE (Dean et al., 2021), CLaSS (Das et al., 2021), and HydrAMP (Szymczak et al., 2023) reconstructed the sequences from latent space according to the encoder-decoder architecture of variational autoencoders (VAEs)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Das et al., 2021.

claim: HydrAMP reconstructed sequences from latent space according to the encoder-decoder architecture of variational autoencoders.
source: Generative models like PepVAE (Dean et al., 2021), CLaSS (Das et al., 2021), and HydrAMP (Szymczak et al., 2023) reconstructed the sequences from latent space according to the encoder-decoder architecture of variational autoencoders (VAEs)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Szymczak et al., 2023.

claim: PepGAN utilized the generative adversarial network (GAN) to approximate antimicrobial sequences by deceiving the discriminator.
source: while PepGAN (Tucs et al., 2020) and AMPGAN v2 (Van Oort et al., 2021) utilized the generative adversarial network (GAN) to approximate the antimicrobial sequences by deceiving the discriminator.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tucs et al., 2020.

claim: AMPGAN v2 utilized the generative adversarial network (GAN) to approximate antimicrobial sequences by deceiving the discriminator.
source: while PepGAN (Tucs et al., 2020) and AMPGAN v2 (Van Oort et al., 2021) utilized the generative adversarial network (GAN) to approximate the antimicrobial sequences by deceiving the discriminator.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Van Oort et al., 2021.

claim: The sparsity of AMPs in the whole peptide space demands accurate prediction of MIC values for efficient sampling and filtering of AMP analogues.
source: (1) the sparsity of AMPs in the whole peptide space, which demands accurate prediction of MIC values for efficient sampling and filtering of AMP analogues (Szymczak et al., 2023; Pandi et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Szymczak et al., 2023 and Pandi et al., 2023.

claim: Current machine learning predictive models usually perform binary classification tasks instead of giving specific activity values.
source: The current machine learning predictive models usually perform the binary classification task and label the generated sequences as active or not, instead of giving specific activity values.
evidence: This is a general observation about the state of the field.

claim: A popular pipeline combines independent modules of filtering, classification, and regression, but it faces risks of step-wise bias accumulation.
source: To overcome this shortcoming, a popular pipeline combines independent modules of filtering, classification, and regression, but it faces risks of step-wise bias accumulation (Huang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Huang et al., 2023.

claim: The enveloped virus possesses a targetable membrane which closely mimics the phospholipid components of cellular organelles.
source: More importantly, the enveloped virus also possesses a targetable membrane, which closely mimic the phospholipid components of cellular organelles.
evidence: This is established knowledge about viral structure.

claim: The AMP database recorded antiviral activities of at least 2000 antiviral peptides (AVPs).
source: Even though the AMP database recorded antiviral activities of at least 2000 antiviral peptides (AVPs), whether the current models can readily generate AVPs remain elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about database content.

claim: More than 120 AMPs have been suggested by deep learning models in the past three years.
source: To our knowledge, more than 120 AMPs have been suggested by deep learning models in the past three years, only a fraction of these studies demonstrated animal results.
evidence: This is a summary of recent literature.

claim: Only a fraction of deep learning-suggested AMPs have demonstrated animal results.
source: To our knowledge, more than 120 AMPs have been suggested by deep learning models in the past three years, only a fraction of these studies demonstrated animal results.
evidence: This is an observation about the state of the field.

claim: The study presented a new deep learning-based de novo AMP design framework consisting of a GAN generator and an antimicrobial activity regressor named AMPredictor.
source: In the current study, we addressed these shortcomings and presented a new deep learning-based de novo AMP design framework, consisting of a GAN generator and an antimicrobial activity regressor named AMPredictor.
evidence: This describes the methodology of the study.

claim: The graph convolution network (GCN) of AMPredictor allowed effective training of a regression model for the task of MIC predictions.
source: The graph convolution network (GCN) of AMPredictor allowed us to effectively train a regression model for the task of MIC predictions.
evidence: This describes a feature of the methodology.

claim: Three top-ranking sequences (P001, P002, and P076) were selected and evaluated for their efficacies against different pathogens.
source: Through in-depth investigations of generated sequences (e.g., antiviral possibilities), we selected three top-ranking sequences (P001, P002, and P076) and evaluated their efficacies against different pathogens (four drug-resistant bacteria and five enveloped virus).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach of the study.

claim: P076 outperformed polymyxin B in terms of safety and efficacy in mouse models.
source: It also outperformed a clinically relevant antibiotic polymyxin B (PB) in terms of safety and efficacy, as evaluated in mouse models.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: P002 broadly neutralized viruses in cellular infection models.
source: Another peptide P002 broadly neutralized viruses in cellular infection models.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: The designed peptides inhibited a spectrum of pathogens but with delicate preferences toward bacterial or viral species.
source: We challenged our computational models to generate bifunctional AMPs, and our results demonstrated that these peptides inhibited a spectrum of pathogens, but with delicate preferences toward bacterial or viral species.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on experimental data.

claim: The GAN module was trained with 3280 AMP sequences to capture the pattern of AMPs through few-shot learning.
source: We trained the GAN module with 3280 AMP sequences to capture the pattern of AMPs through few-shot learning.
evidence: This describes the training methodology.

claim: The training goal of GAN is to reach a relative balance between the generator and discriminator.
source: The training goal of GAN is to reach a relative balance between the generator and discriminator (see Equation 1).
evidence: This is established knowledge about GAN training supported by citation.

claim: The generator takes random noise as input to produce fake samples which are fed into the discriminator along with real data.
source: The generator takes random noise as input to produce fake samples, which are fed into the discriminator along with the real data.
evidence: This describes the GAN architecture used in the study.

claim: The discriminator tries to distinguish between real and fake data and returns a probability to update the weights of the networks.
source: The discriminator tries to distinguish between the real and fake data, then returns a probability to update the weights of the networks (Goodfellow et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about GANs supported by citation to Goodfellow et al., 2014.

claim: The study employed amino acid factors (AAFs) to encode peptide sequences and describe their physicochemical features.
source: Here, we employed a low-dimensional vector called amino acid factors (AAFs) to encode the peptide sequences and describe their physicochemical features (Atchley et al., 2005).
evidence: This describes the encoding method used, supported by citation.

claim: The distributions of newly sampled sequences among existing AMPs were clearly observed after mapping peptide AAF features onto two-dimensional space using UMAP and t-SNE.
source: We clearly observed the distributions of newly sampled sequences among the existing AMPs after mapping peptide AAF features onto the two-dimensional space (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is supported by Figure 1b showing the visualization results.

claim: With iterating and updating, the generator learns the feature distribution of actual data and generates diverse sequences.
source: With iterating and updating, the generator learns the feature distribution of actual data and generates diverse sequences.
evidence: This describes the training process and outcome.

claim: The identity of each generated sequence was around 0.35 to the known database, indicating a low level of similarity to existing AMPs.
source: We found the identity of each generated sequence was around 0.35 to the known database (Figure 1c), indicating a low level of similarity to the existing AMPs.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Generated peptides hold similar physiochemical features to real AMPs as evidenced by six descriptors.
source: With distinct sequence compositions, generated peptides still hold similar physiochemical features to real AMPs, as evidenced by six descriptors of aliphatic index, aromaticity, net charge, the ratio of hydrophobic amino acids, instability index, and isoelectric point (Figure 1d; Müller et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1d and citation.

claim: AMPredictor is a GCN-based regression model equivalent to the 'score function' in virtual drug screen.
source: We then developed an independent module AMPredictor to estimate the MIC values of arbitrary peptide sequences. AMPredictor is a GCN-based regression model, equivalent to the 'score function' in virtual drug screen.
evidence: This describes the model architecture and purpose.

claim: AMPredictor uses graph representation of peptides with amino acid residues as graph nodes and predicted contact maps as graph edges.
source: We chose graph as the representation of peptides, with their amino acid residues as graph nodes and the predicted contact maps as graph edges.
evidence: This describes the model input representation.

claim: The node features in AMPredictor were embeddings from the protein language model ESM.
source: The node features were embeddings from the protein language model ESM (Rives et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes the feature encoding method, supported by citation.

claim: AMPredictor obtained a low RMSE of 0.5348 and a high Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.7072 on the test set.
source: AMPredictor obtained a low root mean squared error (RMSE) of 0.5348 and a high Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) of 0.7072 on the test set (10% size of the dataset) (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is a performance metric from the study shown in Figure 1e (likely a typo in the text referring to Figure 1b).

claim: AMPredictor obtained the best performance in comparison to its ablating versions by integrating representations of residual-level, sequence-level, and protein structural-level information.
source: By integrating the representations of residual-level, sequence-level, and protein structural-level information, AMPredictor obtained the best performance in comparison to its ablating versions (Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This is supported by ablation study results in Supplementary file 1a.

claim: The context embeddings from ESM play vital roles in predicting MICs.
source: The ablation study indicated that the context embeddings from ESM play vital roles in predicting MICs, and the contact map assisted in improvement despite it being a simplified representation of protein structure.
evidence: This is a finding from the ablation study.

claim: The contact map assisted in improvement of MIC prediction despite being a simplified representation of protein structure.
source: The ablation study indicated that the context embeddings from ESM play vital roles in predicting MICs, and the contact map assisted in improvement despite it being a simplified representation of protein structure.
evidence: This is a finding from the ablation study.

claim: AMPredictor outperforms five baseline methods (MLP, CNN, GRU, LSTM, and Transformer) in terms of accuracy at predicting antimicrobial activity values.
source: We also compared the performance of AMPredictor with five typical deep neural networks as baselines, including the multilayer perceptron (MLP), convolutional neural network (CNN), gated recurrent unit (GRU), long short-term memory (LSTM), and Transformer. AMPredictor outperforms these methods in terms of accuracy at the task of predicting antimicrobial activity values (scatter plots in Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by comparison results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Both bacterial membranes and viral envelopes are potential targets of AMPs.
source: Our study was based on the hypothesis that both bacterial membranes and viral envelopes were potential targets of AMPs, and the dual-function of antibacterial and antiviral could be encoded into one peptide sequence.
evidence: This is the hypothesis of the study.

claim: The dual-function of antibacterial and antiviral could be encoded into one peptide sequence.
source: Our study was based on the hypothesis that both bacterial membranes and viral envelopes were potential targets of AMPs, and the dual-function of antibacterial and antiviral could be encoded into one peptide sequence.
evidence: This is the hypothesis of the study.

claim: Generator v1 was trained solely on collected AMP sequences.
source: The generator v1 was trained solely on collected AMP sequences, and generator v2 was trained on the AMP set and known 1788 AVPs from AVPdb.
evidence: This describes the training data for generator v1.

claim: Generator v2 was trained on the AMP set and known 1788 AVPs from AVPdb.
source: The generator v1 was trained solely on collected AMP sequences, and generator v2 was trained on the AMP set and known 1788 AVPs from AVPdb.
evidence: This describes the training data for generator v2.

claim: Data curation of AVPdb resulted in only 759 unique AVPs from ~2000 sequences with IC50 labels.
source: As the source data, the AVPdb provided ~2000 sequences with IC50 labels (Qureshi et al., 2015). However, data curation resulted in only 759 unique AVPs.
evidence: This describes the data processing outcome, with citation.

claim: The quantitative data of AVPs were insufficient for training another GCN-based regression model.
source: We determined that the quantitative data of AVPs were insufficient for training another GCN-based regression model.
evidence: This is a determination made by the authors based on data availability.

claim: Binary classification exhibits robustness against noise of a relatively small dataset.
source: Instead, binary classification should exhibit robustness against noise of a relatively small dataset.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about machine learning.

claim: The study used a collective of five published AVP classification tools for making yes/no decisions.
source: Hence, we merely made yes/no decisions using a collective of five published AVP classification tools (AVPpred [Thakur et al., 2012], DeepAVP [Li et al., 2020], Deep-AVPpred [Sharma et al., 2022], ENNAVIA [Timmons and Hewage, 2021], and AI4AVP [Lin et al., 2022], details in Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: This describes the methodology with citations to the tools used.

claim: 1024 new peptides were obtained from each generator.
source: We obtained 1024 new peptides from each generator and kept the sequences with a predicted MIC value of less than 10 µM by AMPredictor.
evidence: This describes the generation and filtering process.

claim: More than 100 peptides passed the ensemble filter of all five AVP classifiers.
source: More than 100 peptides passed the ensemble filter of all five AVP classifiers.
evidence: This is a result from the filtering process.

claim: Generator v2 did not feature a higher passing ratio despite being trained with AVPs.
source: Interestingly, generator v2 did not feature a higher passing ratio, although it was trained with AVPs.
evidence: This is an observation from the study.

claim: 12 peptides from each generator were selected for experimental validation based on hemolysis and other physicochemical properties.
source: Based on their hemolysis and other physicochemical properties, we selected 12 peptides from each generator for experimental validation.
evidence: This describes the selection criteria for experimental validation.

claim: All selected peptides had E-values greater than 0.1 or no hits found when checked for novelty using BLAST.
source: We also checked their novelty using BLAST with the training set or DRAMP database, and all their E-values are greater than 0.1 or no hits found (Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: This is supported by BLAST results in Supplementary file 1c.

claim: All 24 peptides exhibited effective antibacterial capability in inhibiting six different strains involving three MDR species.
source: All 24 peptides exhibited effective antibacterial capability in inhibiting six different strains involving three MDR species (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Several peptides obtained remarkable MIC values of less than 1 µM, such as P026 and P036.
source: Several peptides obtained remarkable MIC values of less than 1 µM, such as P026 and P036, indicating the effectiveness of our generator for de novo designing AMPs.
evidence: This is an experimental result from the study.

claim: There were 6 bifunctional AMPs out of 12 from generator v1.
source: There were 6 and 7 bifunctional AMPs out of 12 from generators v1 and v2, respectively (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: There were 7 bifunctional AMPs out of 12 from generator v2.
source: There were 6 and 7 bifunctional AMPs out of 12 from generators v1 and v2, respectively (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The antiviral feature was 'naturally' encoded in AMP sequences.
source: Through the comparison between generators v1 and v2, we demonstrated that the antiviral feature was 'naturally' encoded in AMP sequences.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the two generators.

claim: 104 novel peptides were acquired via the de novo design framework.
source: We acquired 104 novel peptides via the de novo design framework.
evidence: This describes the output of the design process.

claim: 42 peptides were predicted to have MIC values below 10 µM.
source: Among them, 42 and 26 were predicted to own MIC values below 10 µM and 5 µM, respectively (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by predictions listed in Supplementary file 2.

claim: 26 peptides were predicted to have MIC values below 5 µM.
source: Among them, 42 and 26 were predicted to own MIC values below 10 µM and 5 µM, respectively (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by predictions listed in Supplementary file 2.

claim: 32 peptides met the criteria of being regarded as antiviral candidates (four or more positive votes).
source: We regarded a peptide as an antiviral candidate if four or more positive votes were recorded and 32 peptides met our criteria.
evidence: This describes the filtering outcome.

claim: Three potent peptides P001, P002, and P076 were picked through ranking of high activity and low toxicity.
source: Through the ranking of high activity and low toxicity, we picked three potent peptides P001, P002, and P076 (Figure 1f), all of which featured amphiphilic signatures of sequence and enriched cationic regions (e.g., helical wheel projections in Figure 1—figure supplement 3), for in vitro and in vivo experimental assessment.
evidence: This describes the selection process, supported by Figure 1f and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: P001, P002, and P076 all featured amphiphilic signatures of sequence and enriched cationic regions.
source: Through the ranking of high activity and low toxicity, we picked three potent peptides P001, P002, and P076 (Figure 1f), all of which featured amphiphilic signatures of sequence and enriched cationic regions (e.g., helical wheel projections in Figure 1—figure supplement 3), for in vitro and in vivo experimental assessment.
evidence: This is supported by helical wheel projections in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: All three peptides (P001, P002, and P076) exhibited inspiring bactericidal properties with MICs ranging from 0.20 to 15.18 μM.
source: All the peptides exhibited inspiring bactericidal properties with MICs ranging from 0.20 to 15.18 μM (corresponding to 0.625–40 µg/mL, Figure 3a).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: P001 showed broad-spectrum antibacterial capability with MICs less than 4 μM across all eight strains of four bacteria species.
source: P001 showed broad-spectrum antibacterial capability with MICs less than 4 μM across all the eight strains of four bacteria species.
evidence: This is an experimental result from the study.

claim: P002 featured lower MIC values in inhibiting Gram-positive bacteria S. aureus.
source: P002 featured lower MIC values in inhibiting Gram-positive bacteria S. aureus, while P076 mainly inhibits Gram-negative bacteria A. baumannii, E. coli, and P. aeruginosa.
evidence: This is an experimental result from the study.

claim: P076 mainly inhibits Gram-negative bacteria A. baumannii, E. coli, and P. aeruginosa.
source: P002 featured lower MIC values in inhibiting Gram-positive bacteria S. aureus, while P076 mainly inhibits Gram-negative bacteria A. baumannii, E. coli, and P. aeruginosa.
evidence: This is an experimental result from the study.

claim: The experimentally measured MICs against E. coli agreed well with the predictions of AMPredictor.
source: Notably, the experimentally measured MICs against E. coli agreed well with the predictions of AMPredictor (Figure 1f), indicating the accuracy of our regression models.
evidence: This is supported by comparison shown in Figure 1f.

claim: Both P001 and P002 displayed dose-dependent toxicity to mouse erythrocytes with average hemolysis higher than 50% at 20 μM.
source: The hemolytic analysis revealed that both P001 and P002 displayed dose-dependent toxicity to mouse erythrocytes (Figure 3b), with average hemolysis higher than 50% at high concentrations (20 μM, or 100 µg/mL).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: The hemolysis of P076 was lower than 1% at concentrations up to 70 μM.
source: Nevertheless, the hemolysis of P076 was lower than 1% at concentrations up to 70 μM.
evidence: This is an experimental result from the study.

claim: CC50 values of all three peptides were well above 30 μM for three mammalian cell lines.
source: We also inspected the apparent cytotoxicity (CC50) of three peptides on three mammalian cell lines (Vero-E6, A549, Huh-7) using CCK8 assays. For the cell cultures, CC50 values of all three peptides were well above 30 μM (Figure 4—figure supplement 3a).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3a.

claim: The CC50 of P076 ranged from 35.5 μM (for A549 cells) to 66.8 μM (for Huh-7 cells).
source: The CC50 of P076, specifically, were in the range of 35.5 μM (for A549 cells from lung tissues) to 66.8 μM (for Huh-7 cells from liver tissues).
evidence: This is an experimental result from the study.

claim: All three peptides are potential candidates for inhibiting the clinically relevant A. baumannii.
source: Our data suggest that all three peptides are potential candidates for inhibiting the clinically relevant A. baumannii, which is a top-ranking pathogen with critical priority for development of new antibiotics, as defined by WHO (De Oliveira et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data and citation.

claim: A. baumannii is a top-ranking pathogen with critical priority for development of new antibiotics, as defined by WHO.
source: Our data suggest that all three peptides are potential candidates for inhibiting the clinically relevant A. baumannii, which is a top-ranking pathogen with critical priority for development of new antibiotics, as defined by WHO (De Oliveira et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to De Oliveira et al., 2020.

claim: The MIC of P076 at eliminating MDRAB reached 0.21 μM, half of P001 (0.40 μM) and P002 (0.47 μM).
source: The MIC of P076 at eliminating the persistent MDRAB reached 0.21 μM, a value half of P001 and P002 (0.40 and 0.47 μM, respectively).
evidence: This is an experimental result from the study.

claim: P076 was comparable with P001 but more efficient than P002 against E. coli and P. aeruginosa.
source: Meanwhile, P076 was comparable with P001 but more efficient than P002 against E. coli and P. aeruginosa.
evidence: This is an experimental result from the study.

claim: The P076 concentration to induce 50% death in mice was calculated to be 80 mg/kg, approximately threefold higher than that of PB (26 mg/kg).
source: The P076 concentration to induce a 50% death was calculated to be 80 mg/kg, approximately threefold higher than that of PB (26 mg/kg, Figure 3c).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: No pathological changes were observed in the liver, spleen, and kidneys of mice given 32 mg/kg P076 after 12 h.
source: H&E staining further verified that no pathological changes were observed in the mice liver, spleen, and kidneys of mice given 32 mg/kg P076 after 12 h, whereas an apparent renal tubular injury was discovered in PB-treated mouse (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by H&E staining results shown in Figure 3d and Figure 3—figure supplement 1a.

claim: An apparent renal tubular injury was discovered in PB-treated mouse.
source: H&E staining further verified that no pathological changes were observed in the mice liver, spleen, and kidneys of mice given 32 mg/kg P076 after 12 h, whereas an apparent renal tubular injury was discovered in PB-treated mouse (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by H&E staining results shown in Figure 3d and Figure 3—figure supplement 1a.

claim: 50% of the mice treated with P076 remained alive after 48 h in the peritoneal infection model, while all mice given PBS or CIP deceased.
source: The mice given PBS (blank buffer) or CIP all deceased after 48 h, while 50% of the mice treated with P076 remained alive (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is supported by survival data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: The bacterial colonization in the peritoneal lavage fluid of PBS-treated mouse was 1.1 × 10^6 CFU, 25 times higher than that in mice treated with P076 (4.2 × 10^4 CFU).
source: Additional investigations revealed that the bacterial colonization in the peritoneal lavage fluid of PBS-treated mouse was averagely 1.1 × 106 CFU, which was 25 times higher than that in the mice treated with P076 (4.2 × 104 CFU, p<0.001), whereas CIP featured less of effect on the number of bacteria (Figure 3f).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3f.

claim: P076 dramatically decreased the bacterial loads in the mouse spleen (about seven times lower).
source: Similarly, P076 dramatically decreased the bacterial loads in the mouse spleen (about seven times lower, Figure 3g, Figure 3—figure supplement 1b), thus demonstrating the prospect of P076 to be developed into a new antibiotic.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3g and Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claim: A cohort of traditional AMPs have been rediscovered with antiviral abilities.
source: A cohort of traditional AMPs have been rediscovered with antiviral abilities (Liu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liu et al., 2022.

claim: The membrane-disrupting capacity of AMPs can adapt to both bacterial membranes and viral envelopes.
source: One significant reason is that their membrane-disrupting capacity can adapt to both bacterial membranes and viral envelopes, which may be captured by AMPredictor and AVP classifier filters.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mechanism of AMPs.

claim: The experiments included five typical enveloped viruses: CHIKV, HTNV, DENV-2, HSV-1, and SARS-CoV-2 (BA.2 omicron variant).
source: Our experiments included five typical enveloped viruses. Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), Hantaan virus (HTNV), Dengue virus 2 (DENV-2), Herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2, and the BA.2. omicron variant) are all pathogens of the past or ongoing epidemics
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: CHIKV, HTNV, DENV-2, HSV-1, and SARS-CoV-2 are all pathogens of past or ongoing epidemics.
source: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), Hantaan virus (HTNV), Dengue virus 2 (DENV-2), Herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2, and the BA.2. omicron variant) are all pathogens of the past or ongoing epidemics, such as the chikungunya fever, hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, dengue, encephalitis, and COVID-19.
evidence: This is established knowledge about these viruses.

claim: qRT-PCR suggested dose-dependent inhibition of viral-specific gene expressions by P001, P002, and P076.
source: At the mRNA level, the quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) suggested dose-dependent inhibition of viral-specific gene expressions (E1 gene for CHIKV, S gene for HTNV, VP16 gene for HSV-1, NS5a gene for DENV-2, ORF for SARS-CoV-2, Figure 4a, Figure 4—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4a and Figure 4—figure supplement 1b.

claim: P002 nearly abolished all viral infections at 12.5 μM.
source: Corroborating with the qRT-PCR results, P002 nearly abolished all viral infections at 12.5 μM (Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplements 1a and 2).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4b and supplementary figures.

claim: P002 exhibited the highest antiviral potential with EC50 of 0.37 μM (against CHIKV) to 2.08 μM (against HTNV).
source: Among the three peptides, P002 exhibited the highest potential with EC50 of 0.37 μM (against CHIKV) to 2.08 μM (against HTNV) (Figure 4b, Supplementary file 1d).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4b and Supplementary file 1d.

claim: The EC50 of P076 and P001 were in the range of 1.62–2.67 μM (except for inhibiting DENV-2).
source: The EC50 of P076 and P001 were in the range of 1.62–2.67 μM (except for inhibiting DENV-2).
evidence: This is an experimental result from the study.

claim: P135 and P244 were active broad-spectrum AVPs against four viruses as shown by immunofluorescence and qRT-PCR results.
source: Additionally, we tested the antiviral effects of P135 and P244 from our second round of generation. Both the immunofluorescence and qRT-PCR results showed that these AMPs were active broad-spectrum AVPs against four viruses (Figure 4—figure supplement 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: P135 showed significant inhibition on DENV-2 with an EC50 of 0.09 μM.
source: In particular, these two AMPs showed a significant inhibition on DENV-2, for which P135 obtained an EC50 of 0.09 μM (Supplementary file 1d).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Supplementary file 1d.

claim: The SI of P002 against four viruses are 149.21, 31.75, 51.05, and 59.01, three of which outperformed the SI of P001 and P076.
source: The SI of P002 against four viruses are 149.21, 31.75, 51.05, and 59.01, three of which outperformed the SI of P001 and P076, especially for the case of HTNV.
evidence: This is based on calculations from experimental data in Supplementary file 1e.

claim: When viruses were mixed with 10 µM P002 before addition to cells, viral particles became absent while cell morphology kept intact.
source: When the viruses were mixed with 10 µM P002 before addition to the cells, the viral particles became absent while the cell morphology kept intact, indicating the broad-spectrum inhibition effects of P002 (Figure 5c and d).
evidence: This is supported by transmission electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5c and d.

claim: All-atom molecular dynamics simulations were performed with molecular models of bacterial membranes and viral envelopes.
source: We performed all-atom molecular dynamics simulations with molecular models of bacterial membranes and viral envelopes, placed each peptide adjacent to the phospholipid bilayers, and simulated them attaching to the membrane (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a and b).
evidence: This describes the computational methodology, supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1a and b.

claim: For the model of Gram-negative bacteria systems, MM/PBSA calculations and ∆Gbind distinguished P002 from P076 and P001.
source: For the model of Gram-negative bacteria systems, the MM/PBSA calculations and ∆Gbind distinguished P002 from P076 and P001 (Supplementary file 1j).
evidence: This is supported by computational results in Supplementary file 1j.

claim: Evaluated by ∆Gbind (–465.79 ± 11.39 kJ/mol), P076 would associate with the membrane of Gram-negative bacteria tighter than others.
source: Evaluated by ∆Gbind (–465.79 ± 11.39 kJ/mol), P076 would associate with the membrane of Gram-negative bacteria tighter than others.
evidence: This is a computational result from the study.

claim: For the model of viral envelopes, all binding energies were weaker than that to bacteria.
source: For the model of viral envelopes, all binding energies were weaker than that to bacteria.
evidence: This is a computational result from the study.

claim: More P076 and P001 peptides were recruited to immobilized LPS than P002 at 500 nM.
source: More P076 and P001 peptides were recruited to immobilized LPS than that of P002 at 500 nM (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is supported by BLI data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: P076 bound to lipid A at an equilibrium dissociation constant (KD) of 56.1 nM.
source: Further experiments demonstrated that P076 bound to lipid A, the innermost part of LPS, at an equilibrium dissociation constant (KD) of 56.1 nM.
evidence: This is an experimental result from the study.

claim: The binding affinity of P076 to lipid A was slightly higher than that of P001 (65.7 nM) and approximately 2.4-fold less than that of P002 (135 nM).
source: This binding affinity of P076 to lipid A was slightly higher than that of P001 (65.7 nM) and was approximately 2.4-fold less than that of P002 (135 nM, Figure 6a).
evidence: This is supported by BLI data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: P076 elicited a stronger membrane penetration relative to P001 and P002 in the NPN uptake assay.
source: Then we directly investigated the membrane permeability by 1-N-phenylnaphthylamine (NPN) uptake assay. NPN is a fluorescent dye for detecting the impaired outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria. P076 elicited a stronger membrane penetration relative to P001 and P002 (wavelength scanning in Figure 6c).
evidence: This is supported by NPN uptake assay data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: P002 and P076 gradually inserted into the outer leaflet and represented poses binding to LPS at 100 ns in MD simulations.
source: During the simulation processes, P002 and P076 gradually inserted into the outer leaflet and represented poses binding to LPS at 100 ns (Figure 6e).
evidence: This is supported by MD simulation data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: The distance metric between peptide center of mass and lipid A phosphorus atoms of P002 and P076 declined to less than 2 nm from initial value of about 4 nm.
source: We also measured the distance between the center of mass of peptide and phosphorus atoms of lipid A on z-axis in the latter 50 ns of trajectories (Figure 6d). Compared with the initial value about 4 nm (showing as dashed line), this metric of P002 and P076 declined to less than 2 nm.
evidence: This is supported by MD simulation data shown in Figure 6d.

claim: P001 performed weaker interactions with LPS with an increasing distance in MD simulations.
source: Nevertheless, P001 performed weaker interactions with an increasing distance, which was consistent with the membrane-disrupting experiment in Figure 6c.
evidence: This is a computational result consistent with experimental data.

claim: Three AMPs tended to attach to the membrane in MD simulations with lipid bilayer system mimicking the inner membranes of Gram-negative bacteria.
source: Moreover, three AMPs tended to attach to the membrane in the MD simulations with lipid bilayer system mimicking the inner membranes of Gram-negative bacteria (Figure 5—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by MD simulation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The AMP dataset was collected from PepVAE containing 3280 AMP sequences with their MICs in logarithmic form.
source: Our AMP dataset is collected from PepVAE (Dean et al., 2021) , containing 3280 AMP sequences with their MICs in logarithmic form.
evidence: This describes the data source with citation.

claim: Only AMPs inhibiting E. coli were selected from the dataset.
source: To integrate various AMP sequence and bioactivity data, Witten et al. developed the Giant Repository of AMP Activity (Witten and Witten, 2019). Since the MIC values change when targeting different microbial strains, only AMPs inhibiting E. coli are selected.
evidence: This describes the data curation process with citation.

claim: Peptides without modifications were filtered so that no cysteine appears in the dataset.
source: Also, to simplify the input and reduce accidental effect, peptides without modifications are filtered so that no cysteine appears (amino acid composition in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This describes the data filtering process.

claim: The sequence length of AMPs is less than 40 amino acids, and the majority of lengths (~60%) are between 10 and 20.
source: The sequence length of AMPs is less than 40 amino acids, and the majority of lengths (~60%) are between 10 and 20 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claim: The dataset was divided into training, validation, and testing sets in a ratio of 8:1:1 randomly.
source: During the training process, the dataset is divided into the training, validation, and testing sets in a ratio of 8:1:1 randomly.
evidence: This describes the data splitting methodology.

claim: The entire AMP dataset (3280 sequences) was used for training the generator v1.
source: The entire AMP dataset (3280 sequences) is used for training the generator v1.
evidence: This describes the training data for generator v1.

claim: AVPs with lengths of more than 60 amino acids were excluded from the AVP dataset.
source: The AVP dataset for training the generator v2 is collected from AVPdb (accessed in August 2023). AVPs with lengths of more than 60 amino acids are excluded.
evidence: This describes the data filtering process.

claim: After removing overlaps with the AMP dataset, 1788 AVPs were kept and added to the training set of generator v2.
source: After removing overlaps with the AMP dataset, 1788 AVPs are kept and added to the training set of generator v2.
evidence: This describes the data processing for generator v2.

claim: The GAN architecture utilized three layers of 2D convolution inside both the generator and discriminator.
source: The GAN architecture was utilized to generate novel AMP sequences, where three layers of 2D convolution were inside both the generator and discriminator (Tzu-Tang et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes the model architecture with citation.

claim: Loss function was modified with the Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) strategy to avoid mode collapse.
source: Loss function modified with the Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) strategy was taken to avoid mode collapse, and the optimizer was kept as RMSProp.
evidence: This describes the training methodology.

claim: The learning rate for GAN training was 1e-4.
source: The learning rate was 1e-4.
evidence: This is a training hyperparameter.

claim: Cross training ratio between generator and discriminator was set as 1:5.
source: Cross training ratio between generator and discriminator was set as 1:5.
evidence: This is a training hyperparameter.

claim: Deep learning-based models were trained on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti GPU.
source: Deep learning-based models were trained on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti GPU.
evidence: This describes the computational resources used.

claim: AMPredictor was built based on PyTorch and PyTorch Geometric library.
source: AMPredictor was built based on PyTorch and PyTorch Geometric library.
evidence: This describes the software framework used.

claim: All input sequences were treated with padded zeros to reach unified lengths of 60 in AMPredictor.
source: All input sequences were treated with padded zeros to reach unified lengths of 60.
evidence: This describes the data preprocessing.

claim: RDKit was used to transform each amino acid into 2048-bit Morgan fingerprint in peptide sequences.
source: For chemical fingerprint, RDKit (https://www.rdkit.org/) was used to transform each amino acid into 2048-bit Morgan fingerprint in peptide sequences.
evidence: This describes the feature encoding method.

claim: Pretrained language model esm1b_t33_650M_UR50S was used to provide the embeddings and the contact maps.
source: Pretrained language model esm1b_t33_650M_UR50S was used to provide the embeddings and the contact maps.
evidence: This describes the feature extraction method.

claim: The optimizer for AMPredictor training was Adam.
source: During the training process, the optimizer was Adam, and loss function was the mean squared loss.
evidence: This is a training hyperparameter.

claim: The loss function for AMPredictor was the mean squared loss.
source: During the training process, the optimizer was Adam, and loss function was the mean squared loss.
evidence: This is a training hyperparameter.

claim: Batch size and learning rate for AMPredictor were decided upon grid-search with values of 128 and 0.001, respectively.
source: Batch size and learning rate were decided upon grid-search, whose values were 128 and 0.001, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is supported by grid search results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1c.

claim: All peptides were synthesized by DGpeptide Co., Ltd. with 95% purity via solid-phase peptide synthesis procedures.
source: All the peptides were synthesized by DGpeptide Co., Ltd. with 95% purity via solid-phase peptide synthesis procedures.
evidence: This describes the peptide synthesis methodology.

claim: Mass spectrometry was used to verify the molecular weights of synthesized peptides.
source: Mass spectrometry was used to verify the molecular weights (Figure 2—figure supplements 1–25).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplements 1–25.

claim: MICs were determined using the broth microdilution method recommended by the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute with modifications reported by the Hancock Laboratory.
source: The minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of peptides against bacteria including A. baumannii (ATCC 17978), multidrug-resistant A. baumannii (MDRAB) (Wang et al., 2018), S. aureus (ATCC 25923), methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA, ATCC 43300), E. coli (ATCC 25922), multidrug-resistant E. coli (MDREC) (Zhao et al., 2019), P. aeruginosa (PAO1), and multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa (MDPRA) (Gao et al., 2020) were determined using the broth microdilution method recommended by the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute with modifications reported by the Hancock Laboratory (Wu and Hancock, 1999).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology with citations.

claim: The recorded MIC was the lowest concentration of peptides causing a 70% reduction in bacterial turbidity.
source: The recorded MIC was the lowest concentration of peptides, causing a 70% reduction in bacterial turbidity.
evidence: This defines the MIC measurement criterion.

claim: Vero-E6, A549, and Huh-7 cell lines were purchased from the National Collection of Authenticated Cell Cultures.
source: Vero-E6 (African green monkey kidney cell line), Huh-7 (hepatocellular carcinoma cell line), and A549 (human lung carcinoma cell line) were purchased from the National Collection of Authenticated Cell Cultures (serials: SCSP-520, SCSP-503, and SCSP-526).
evidence: This describes the cell line sources.

claim: The STR typing results of the cell DNA showed clear amplification profiles and reliable typing results, and the mycoplasma detection result was negative.
source: The STR typing results of the cell DNA showed clear amplification profiles and reliable typing results, and the mycoplasma detection result was negative.
evidence: This describes the cell line authentication results.

claim: HSV-1 and CHIKV were propagated in Vero-E6 cells.
source: HSV-1 and CHIKV were propagated in Vero-E6 cells.
evidence: This describes the virus propagation methodology.

claim: DENV-2 and HTNV were propagated in Huh-7 and A549 cells, respectively.
source: DENV-2 and HTNV were propagated in Huh-7 and A549 cells, respectively.
evidence: This describes the virus propagation methodology.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 were propagated in HeLa-hACE2 cells.
source: SARS-CoV-2 were propagated in HeLa-hACE2 cells.
evidence: This describes the virus propagation methodology.

claim: The CC50 represents the peptide concentration at 50% of viability of uninfected cells.
source: The CC50 represents the peptide concentration at the 50% of viability of uninfected cells.
evidence: This defines the CC50 measurement.

claim: Animal experiments were conducted with approval from the Animal Experimental Ethics Committee of the Army Medical University (AMUWEC20223290).
source: Animal experiments were conducted with approval from the Animal Experimental Ethics Committee of the Army Medical University (AMUWEC20223290).
evidence: This describes the ethical approval for animal experiments.

claim: The Octet Red96 BLI platform was utilized to measure the binding kinetics of three peptides to lipid A.
source: The Octet Red96 BLI platform (Sartorius BioAnalytical Instruments, Bohemia, USA) was utilized to measure the binding kinetics of three peptides to lipid A (L5399, Sigma, Shanghai, China).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology with citations.

claim: The equilibrium dissociation constant (KD) was defined as the division of dissociation rate constant (Koff) and the association rate constant (Kon).
source: The equilibrium dissociation constant (KD) was defined as the division of dissociation rate constant (Koff) and the association rate constant (Kon).
evidence: This defines the KD calculation.

claim: The initial structures of peptides were built via AlphaFold2 single-sequence version.
source: The initial structures of peptides were built via AlphaFold2 single-sequence version (Mirdita et al., 2022).
evidence: This describes the structure prediction methodology with citation.

claim: Lipid bilayer models were constructed using CHARMM-GUI server.
source: Lipid bilayer models were constructed using CHARMM-GUI server, along with placing parallel peptides approximately 2 nm above the membrane surface (Wu et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the model building methodology with citation.

claim: Nine systems were built for three peptides versus three kinds of lipid bilayers (viral envelopes, Gram-negative bacterial inner membranes and outer membranes).
source: Nine systems were built for three peptides versus three kinds of lipid bilayers (viral envelopes, Gram-negative bacterial inner membranes and outer membranes) (Liu et al., 2022; Allsopp et al., 2022).
evidence: This describes the simulation systems with citations.

claim: All-atom MD simulations were performed using GROMACS 2021.2 with the CHARMM36 force field and the TIP3P water model for 100 ns, with a time step of 2 fs.
source: All-atom MD simulations were performed using GROMACS 2021.2 with the CHARMM36 force field and the TIP3P water model for 100 ns, with a time step of 2 fs (Best et al., 2012; Klauda et al., 2010).
evidence: This describes the simulation methodology with citations.

claim: Three independent runs were performed for each MD simulation system.
source: Three independent runs were performed for each system.
evidence: This describes the simulation replication.

claim: Binding free energy was calculated using the molecular mechanics Poisson-Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) method on average of extracted 20 frames from the last 20 ns.
source: Binding free energy was calculated using the molecular mechanics Poisson-Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) method on average of extracted 20 frames from the last 20 ns.
evidence: This describes the binding energy calculation methodology.

claim: The dielectric constant was set as 7 for phospholipids and the entropy term was neglected in MM/PBSA calculations.
source: Following a previous study, the dielectric constant was set as 7 for phospholipids and the entropy term was neglected (Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the calculation parameters with citation.
